questions.stem: Does the following graph have an Euler circuit?  (Graph not shown)
questions.solution: An Euler circuit exists in a graph if and only if all its vertices have even degree. In this case, the graph has no vertices with odd degree, indicating an Euler circuit is present.
questions.explanation: Euler's circuit theorem states that a connected graph has an Euler circuit if and only if all its vertices are of even degree. If there are more than two vertices with odd degree, the graph cannot have an Euler circuit.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to assume that 'even number of vertices with odd degree' is sufficient for an Euler circuit. However, it's the degrees of the vertices that matter, not their count.

questions.stem: Does the following graph have an Euler path?  (Graph not shown)
questions.solution: An Euler path exists in a graph if and only if exactly two vertices have odd degree and the graph is connected. In this case, the graph has exactly two vertices with odd degree.
questions.explanation: Euler's path theorem states that a connected graph has an Euler path if and only if exactly two of its vertices have odd degree. If there are more than two vertices with odd degree or the graph is not connected, it cannot have an Euler path.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to assume that 'all its vertices have even degree' guarantees an Euler path. For an Euler path, exactly two vertices must have odd degree.

questions.stem: What is the condition for a graph to have an Euler trail?

choices.B: Exactly one vertex has odd degree.
choices.C: At least two vertices have odd degree and the graph is connected.
choices.D: The graph must be a complete graph.

questions.solution: An Euler trail exists in a graph if and only if at least two vertices have odd degree and the graph is connected. This allows for an alternating sequence of edges that start and end on odd-degree vertices.
questions.explanation: Euler's trail theorem states that a connected graph has an Euler trail if and only if at least two of its vertices have odd degree. The presence of odd-degree vertices enables the formation of a trail that starts and ends at these vertices, alternating between even and odd degrees.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to assume that 'all vertices have even degree' is necessary for an Euler trail, which is actually the condition for an Euler circuit.

questions.stem: In a graph with 10 vertices and 15 edges, how many vertices can have odd degree?
questions.solution: The sum of the degrees of all vertices in a graph is equal to twice the number of edges. In this case, 2 * 15 = 30, which means the total degree sum is 30. Since there are 10 vertices and each vertex can have an even degree, at most two vertices can have odd degrees for the sum to be even.
questions.explanation: In a graph, the sum of the degrees of all its vertices is equal to twice the number of edges (Handshaking Lemma). Given that there are 15 edges, the total degree sum must be 30. For an Euler path or trail to exist, at most two vertices can have odd degrees. Since 30 is an even number and we need to distribute it among 10 vertices, at most two vertices can have an odd sum (e.g., one vertex with degree 1 and another with degree 3).
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to assume that more than two vertices could have odd degrees. The Handshaking Lemma requires an even total degree sum.

questions.stem: What is the difference between an Euler path and an Euler circuit?

choices.A: An Euler circuit must start and end at the same vertex, while an Euler path can start and end at different vertices.
choices.B: Both paths and circuits require all vertices to have even degree.
choices.C: An Euler circuit exists only in connected graphs, but an Euler path does not.
choices.D: The number of odd-degree vertices is irrelevant for both paths and circuits.

questions.solution: An Euler circuit must start and end at the same vertex, while an Euler path can start and end at different vertices. Both require specific conditions on the degrees of their vertices: exactly two odd- degree vertices for a path and all even-degree vertices for a circuit.
questions.explanation: The key difference between an Euler path and an Euler circuit is that an Euler circuit must form a closed loop, starting and ending at the same vertex, while an Euler path can start and end at different vertices. Both require specific conditions on the degrees of their vertices: exactly two odd-degree vertices for a path and all even-degree vertices for a circuit.

questions.stem: What is the condition for a graph to have an Euler circuit if it is not connected?

choices.A: Each component must have exactly two vertices with odd degree.
choices.B: At least one component must have all even- degree vertices.
choices.C: All components must be complete graphs.

questions.solution: If a graph is not connected and has an Euler circuit, each of its connected components must have exactly two vertices with odd degree. This allows for separate Euler circuits in each component that can be combined into one overall Euler circuit.
questions.explanation: For a disconnected graph to have an Euler circuit, each of its connected components must satisfy the conditions for an Euler circuit or path. In this case, since we're looking for a single circuit, each component must have exactly two vertices with odd degree, allowing them to be connected into one continuous circuit.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to assume that all components need even-degree vertices for an Euler circuit in a disconnected graph. However, it's the number of odd- degree vertices per component that matters, not the overall degree distribution.
